'''András Frank''' (born 3 June 1949) is a [[Hungarian people|Hungarian]] [[mathematician]], working in [[combinatorics]], especially in [[graph theory]], and [[combinatorial optimisation]]. He is director of the Institute of Mathematics of the [[ELTE Faculty of Sciences|Faculty of Sciences]] of the [[Eötvös Loránd University]], [[Budapest]].

== Mathematical work==
Using the [[Lenstra–Lenstra–Lovász lattice basis reduction algorithm|LLL-algorithm]], Frank, and his student, [[Éva Tardos]] developed a general method, which could transform some polynomial-time algorithms into strong polynomial.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Frank | first1 = András
 | last2 = Tardos | first2 = Éva
 | doi = 10.1007/BF02579200
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Combinatorica
 | pages = 49–65
 | title = An application of simultaneous diophantine approximation in combinatorial optimization
 | volume = 7
 | year = 1987| s2cid = 45585308
 }}.</ref> He solved the problem of finding the minimum number of edges to be added to a given undirected graph so that in the resulting graph the edge-connectivity between any two vertices ''u'' and ''v'' is at least a predetermined number ''f''(''u'',''v'').<ref>{{citation
 | last = Frank | first = András
 | doi = 10.1137/0405003
 | issue = 1
 | journal = [[SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics]]
 | pages = 25–53
 | title = Augmenting graphs to meet edge-connectivity requirements
 | url = http://www.cs.elte.hu/~frank/cikkek/FrankJ23.PDF
 | volume = 5
 | year = 1992}}.</ref>

== Degrees, awards ==
He received the Candidate of Mathematical Science degree in 1980, advisor: [[László Lovász]],<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=András  Frank|id=26596}}.</ref> and the Doctor of Mathematical Science degree (1990) from the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]]. In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Frank, András|chapter=Applications of relaxed submodularity|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=343–354|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011591000}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Tibor Szele]] Prize of the [[János Bolyai Mathematical Society]] in 2002<ref>[http://www.bolyai.hu/down/2009/SzeleTibor09.pdf Szele Tibor Emlékérem] (in Hungarian). [[János Bolyai Mathematical Society]], retrieved 2010-01-21.</ref> and the [[Albert Szent-Györgyi]] Prize in 2009.<ref name="nam">[http://www.cs.elte.hu/math/news/index.html?lang=en News about mathematics], Eötvös Loránd University,   Faculty of Science,   Institute of Mathematics, retrieved 2010-01-21.</ref> In June 2009 the ELTE Mathematical Institute sponsored a workshop in honor of his 60th birthday.<ref name="nam"/><ref>[http://www.cs.elte.hu/egres/fa60/ Frank András 60. születésnapja alkalmából] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721105552/http://www.cs.elte.hu/egres/fa60/ |date=2011-07-21 }} (in Hungarian), retrieved 2010-01-21.</ref> He is a member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] (corresponding member since 2016, full member since 2022).<ref>[https://mta.hu/koztestuleti_tagok?PersonId=10196 Members of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences' public body: Frank András] (in Hungarian)</ref>
